Hosted byRwanda Development Board (RDB), Visit Rwanda team
Dates2 to 13 September 2026
Who went for usWendy
HighlightThe 21st Kwita Izina Gorilla Naming Ceremony in Kinigi, Musanze, on 4 September
Areas coveredKigali, Akagera National Park, Nyanza and Huye, Nyungwe National Park, Lake Kivu (Rusizi and Karongi), Musanze and Volcanoes National Park

Why this matters for selling This one trip covers the classic Rwanda circuit: city, savannah safari, rainforest, lake and gorillas. It is a ready-made shape for a 10 to 12 day client itinerary, and you can point clients to the trip video to show them what each part looks like.

04

Kwita Izina Explained

Kwita Izina means "to give a name" in Kinyarwanda. It is Rwanda's yearly ceremony for naming the baby mountain gorillas born in Volcanoes National Park, and it is based on the Rwandan tradition of naming a newborn in front of family and community.

The 2026 ceremony
Edition21st, held on Friday 4 September 2026
WhereKinigi, Musanze District, at the foot of Volcanoes National Park
Babies named22 baby mountain gorillas
Theme"Conservation is Life: Sustaining the Future"
Since it began in 2005460 gorillas have now been named through the ceremony

Each baby is named by a guest "namer", from conservationists and local heroes to international sports and music personalities. The day mixes the naming with music, traditional dance and speeches, and it is a big moment for Rwanda's conservation and tourism story.

How to use this with clients Kwita Izina is a great story to share when talking about gorilla trekking: gorilla permit money helps pay for protecting the gorillas and supporting the communities around the park, and the naming ceremony celebrates that every year.
05

Where They Went

Kigali

The starting and finishing point. The group visited the Kigali Genocide Memorial, did a city tour including the Nyandungu Urban Ecopark, and stayed at three different hotels over the trip.

Akagera National Park

Rwanda's savannah safari park in the east. The group took a boat out on Lake Ihema, heard from park management about the park's restoration, and did a full game drive from the south to the north of the park.

Nyanza, Huye and Nyungwe

On the way south they stopped at the King's Palace Museum in Nyanza and the Ethnographic Museum in Huye. Nyungwe National Park is the rainforest: the group did the zipline and the canopy walkway at Uwinka.

Lake Kivu

They stayed at both ends of the lake, first in Rusizi in the south, then in Karongi, driving the scenic Kivu belt road in between. The afternoon boat ride from Karongi was a highlight: island monkeys, fishermen heading out at sunset in their traditional boats, and Ankole cattle (the ones with the huge horns) swimming between the islands.

Musanze and Volcanoes National Park

Home of the mountain gorillas. Besides the ceremony on day 3, the group went gorilla trekking, visited the Ellen DeGeneres Campus of the Dian Fossey Gorilla Fund and the Red Rocks cultural centre, and had a distillery and dinner experience at Virunga Mountain Spirits and Kinigi Table.

Photos still to come We don't have Wendy's own photos for Akagera, Nyungwe or the gorilla trek yet. The trip video covers all three.

07

Visiting the Kigali Genocide Memorial

The Memorial in Gisozi, Kigali, honours the victims of the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi and is the final resting place of more than 250,000 people. Many visitors to Rwanda include it, usually on their first or last day in Kigali.

  • Allow at least an hour and a half for the visit.
  • Entry is free; donations are welcomed.
  • Photos are allowed in the outdoor gardens but not inside the museum.
  • Hours are reduced on the last Saturday of the month for Umuganda, the national community work morning.
Talking to clients about it Keep it simple and respectful. Let clients know it is a moving, important visit, suggest they keep the rest of that day light, and mention that it may not suit young children.
08

Wendy's Selling Notes

The best part of an educational is what the person who went would tell a client. In Wendy's words, the trip was incredible.

How clean and well kept it is

Wendy couldn't believe how clean Rwanda is. The roads are smooth and well looked after, and there is no litter. It's worth telling clients, because it is often not what they expect.

The people

Humble, wonderful people who are very warm and caring. The welcome stays with you.

Gorilla trekking

A fantastic experience, but clients need to be a little fit. It is a heavy walk, so set expectations when you quote it.

Properties I'd sell, and to whom

To add from Wendy

Selling tip from this trip Lead with the gorillas, but sell the whole country: clean, safe-feeling and friendly, with a city, a savannah safari, a rainforest and a lake all within a few hours' drive.
